subject.title: [Bug]: Windows gateway listens but local health/status time out after Telegram polling stall (v2026.5.20)

question: Should repeated unrecovered Telegram/channel stalls escalate to supervised Gateway process recovery, or should OpenClaw keep recovery inside channel/session layers until a current-main affected-host repro identifies the exact blocker?
rationale: The remaining fix could change Gateway process recovery semantics for existing users, and current source plus comments show mitigations without proof that process-level recovery is either necessary or safe.

options.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
options.body: Keep the issue open, collect current-main affected-host logs/proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

options.title: Add Supervised Recovery Policy
options.body: Define and implement a bounded process-level watchdog or exit-on-exhausted-channel-restarts policy with upgrade notes and Windows proof.

options.title: Stay Channel-Scoped
options.body: Reject process-level recovery for now and continue fixing only the specific Telegram, session, and gateway lifecycle failure sources as they are reproduced.

recommendation.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open, collect current-main affected-host logs/proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

likelyOwner.reason: They already performed the targeted repro attempt and authored recent Telegram polling watchdog work, making them the clearest owner for the proof and recovery-policy question.
